name: Aloe Vera

methods.title: Skin application
methods.description: The clear inner gel is commonly applied directly to clean skin as a moisturizing and soothing topical preparation.

methods.title: Minor burns and sunburn
methods.description: A small amount of clear aloe vera gel may be gently applied to minor superficial burns or sun-exposed skin.

methods.title: Hair care
methods.description: Aloe vera gel is commonly used as an ingredient in shampoos, conditioners, and moisturizing hair masks.

warning: For external use, prefer the clear inner gel. Avoid the yellow latex found beneath the leaf skin. Serious burns, deep wounds, or infected skin require professional medical care.

name: Chamomile

methods.title: Herbal infusion
methods.description: Dried chamomile flowers are traditionally steeped in hot water to prepare an herbal infusion.

methods.title: Compress
methods.description: A cooled chamomile infusion may traditionally be used to prepare a gentle external compress.

methods.title: Topical products
methods.description: Chamomile is commonly included in creams, lotions, shampoos, and other cosmetic preparations.

warning: People who are allergic to plants in the daisy family may also react to chamomile.

name: Mint

methods.title: Herbal infusion
methods.description: Fresh or dried mint leaves are commonly steeped in hot water to prepare an herbal infusion.

methods.title: Culinary use
methods.description: Fresh mint leaves are widely used in foods, drinks, sauces, and desserts.

methods.title: Commercial preparations
methods.description: Mint is also found in teas, lozenges, topical products, and other commercially prepared products.

warning: Concentrated peppermint oil is much stronger than ordinary mint leaves and should not be used in the same way. Avoid applying concentrated essential oil directly to the skin.

name: Lavender

methods.title: Herbal infusion
methods.description: Dried lavender flowers may be steeped in hot water to prepare a traditional herbal infusion.

methods.title: Aromatic use
methods.description: Lavender is commonly used in aromatic preparations intended to promote a relaxing environment.

methods.title: Bath and topical products
methods.description: Lavender is frequently included in bath products, creams, lotions, and other cosmetic preparations.

warning: Lavender essential oil is concentrated and should not be confused with ordinary lavender flowers. Skin irritation or allergic reactions may occur in some people.

name: Rosemary

methods.title: Herbal infusion
methods.description: Rosemary leaves are traditionally steeped in hot water to prepare an aromatic herbal infusion.

methods.title: Culinary use
methods.description: Fresh or dried rosemary leaves are commonly used as an aromatic herb in foods and seasonings.

methods.title: Hair care
methods.description: Rosemary is commonly included in shampoos, rinses, and other traditional hair-care preparations.

methods.title: Topical preparations
methods.description: Rosemary extracts may be found in creams, lotions, massage products, and other preparations intended for external use.

warning: Rosemary used as a culinary herb is different from concentrated rosemary extracts or essential oil. Essential oil should not be swallowed or applied undiluted to the skin.

name: Ginger

methods.title: Herbal infusion
methods.description: Fresh or dried ginger may be steeped in hot water to prepare an herbal infusion.

methods.title: Culinary use
methods.description: Fresh, dried, or powdered ginger is widely used as a spice and ingredient in foods and beverages.

methods.title: Commercial preparations
methods.description: Ginger is also available in commercially prepared products such as teas, candies, capsules, and extracts.

warning: Food amounts of ginger are generally well tolerated, but concentrated preparations may cause digestive discomfort and may interact with some medicines.

name: Eucalyptus

methods.title: Aromatic preparations
methods.description: Eucalyptus is traditionally used in aromatic preparations intended to provide a refreshing sensation during periods of nasal or respiratory discomfort.

methods.title: Topical products
methods.description: Eucalyptus extracts or diluted eucalyptus oil may be found in commercially prepared balms, creams, and chest rubs.

methods.title: Commercial respiratory products
methods.description: Eucalyptus is commonly included in products such as lozenges, vapor rubs, and other preparations marketed for respiratory comfort.

warning: Eucalyptus essential oil is highly concentrated and can be toxic if swallowed. It should not be applied undiluted to the skin. Extra caution is required around children.

name: Lemon

methods.title: Food and beverages
methods.description: Fresh lemon juice and fruit are widely used in foods, drinks, and culinary preparations.

methods.title: Warm beverages
methods.description: Lemon juice is commonly added to warm water or herbal infusions as a traditional beverage.

methods.title: Culinary peel
methods.description: Lemon zest may be used in foods and beverages to provide flavor and aroma.

warning: Lemon juice is acidic and frequent direct contact may irritate sensitive skin or contribute to tooth enamel erosion. Citrus oils on the skin may increase sensitivity to sunlight.

name: Asthma Plant

methods.title: Traditional herbal preparations
methods.description: Euphorbia hirta has a history of traditional use in herbal preparations in several regions, particularly for respiratory and digestive complaints.

methods.title: Research use
methods.description: Extracts of the plant have been investigated in laboratory and preclinical research for several biological activities, but these findings do not establish a safe home treatment for serious medical conditions.

warning: Do not use this plant as a substitute for medical treatment of asthma, anaphylaxis, severe breathing problems, or snakebite. These conditions can be medical emergencies. Euphorbia species may also contain irritating plant sap.

name: Passion Flower
alt: Passion flower with purple and white petals

methods.title: Herbal infusion
methods.description: Dried aerial parts of passion flower are traditionally steeped in hot water to prepare an herbal infusion.

methods.title: Commercial preparations
methods.description: Passion flower is also available in commercially prepared herbal teas, extracts, and other standardized products.

warning: Passion flower may cause drowsiness and may increase the effects of medicines or substances that cause sedation. People taking medications should seek professional advice before using medicinal preparations.
